title: Holi: the Lord in the pillar
hookLine: Prahlad says the Lord is even in a stone pillar; his father strikes it, and Narasimha bursts out
carry: the lord is in the pillar, and in everyone
tomorrow: Maha Shivaratri: the great night of Shiva
last: A KING WHO KEPT HIS WORD.

lines: THE FIRE WAS NOT THE END.
cards: At the Holi bonfire, Prahlad walks out of the fire. But the story doesn't stop there, and the Bhagavata Purana carries it further. His father, the king Hiranyakashipu, has tried everything to kill him, and nothing works.
Finally, in a rage, he stands before his son in the great hall and asks: this Vishnu of yours, who you say is everywhere. Is he in this pillar? The boy says yes.
And the king strikes the pillar.

teach.h: NOT MAN OR BEAST, NOT DAY OR NIGHT.
teach.b: To understand what happens next, you need the king's boon. Long before, after fierce austerities, Hiranyakashipu had been granted protection, as the Bhagavata tells it, with a long list of conditions.
No man or animal could kill him. Not by day or by night. Not inside or outside.
Not on the earth or in the sky. Not with any weapon. He thought he'd closed every door.
When he strikes the pillar, it splits open, and out comes Narasimha: Vishnu as half man, half lion. Neither man nor animal.

He seizes the king at twilight, neither day nor night; on the threshold of the hall, neither inside nor outside; across his lap, neither earth nor sky; and ends him with his claws, which are not a weapon.
Narasimha's fury is so terrible that even the gods are afraid to come near. They send the boy. Prahlad bows, and Narasimha calms and puts his hand on his head.
Offered any blessing, Prahlad asks that his father, who tried to kill him again and again, be purified and freed, and the Bhagavata says it is granted.

teach.h: ONLY THE BOY CAN CALM HIM.
teach.b: Under the whole story sits one of Hinduism's biggest teachings: the Lord isn't only in the temple or in heaven.
He is in everything, so fully that he can step out of a stone column.

teach.h: EVEN IN THE PILLAR. EVEN IN HIM.
teach.b: Many teachers read Prahlad's wish the same way: if the Lord is in everyone, he is in the father who hurt him too.
That's why Holi's fire is for Prahlad, and its morning is for visiting, making up, and putting color on old rivals as well as friends.

how: At Holika Dahan, some communities roast ears of new wheat or barley in the bonfire and share them; the next morning, Holi is often a day for visiting, reconciling and starting fresh with neighbors and relatives.

games.q: the rest of Prahlad's story — tap the pairs.

s: Prahlad asks Narasimha to punish his father further
he asks for his father to be purified and freed.
Narasimha is half man, half lion
neither man nor animal, so the boon doesn't hold.
Prahlad's father is defeated by an ordinary weapon
Narasimha uses his claws, which are not a weapon, so the boon doesn't hold.

games.q: you're Prahlad. your father tried to kill you many times. now Narasimha offers you any blessing. what do you ask for?
o: that your father be purified and freed.
games.why: he asks for his father's release, and the Bhagavata says it is granted.

practice: Bring back the small grudge from the fire a couple of weeks ago, or a new one. Try Prahlad's way, just a little: picture the Lord, or simply the good, present in that person too, the way he was present in the pillar.
Then, for one breath, wish them free of whatever made them act that way. If you pray, say it to Narasimha. Let it go with the out-breath.

wordCard.voice: Holi. The fire for Prahlad, Narasimha from the pillar, and a boy who saw the Lord even in the father who hurt him.

orig.note: Sanskrit nara (man) + siṃha (lion): Vishnu as the man-lion.

carryVoice: Your line: the Lord is in the pillar, and in everyone. Tomorrow, a column of fire with no end. Rest well.
